extracted.intended_audience: UW community, researchers, and members of the public interested in peer review and bias in grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and measuring bias in grant peer review processes (how reviewers score proposals and how those scores translate into funding decisions) and designing studies to detect such bias. Includes discussion of proposal-evaluation criteria and statistical approaches to measure bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers rate proposals on criteria such as innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the standard criteria reviewers use to evaluate grant proposals; reviewers give ratings on individual criteria like innovation which contribute to funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers rate proposals on criteria such as soundness of approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators judge methodological rigor and whether the research approach is appropriate and likely to succeed; this is one of the explicit criteria that influences final funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers rate proposals on criteria such as institutional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of the applicant's institutional environment/resources provided as part of proposal evaluation and used in determining funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall rating after individual criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers rate grant proposals along individual criteria, but then assign whatever overall rating they want, favoring whichever criteria they choose to favor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process—individual criterion ratings followed by an unconstrained overall score—can allow reviewers to emphasize different criteria inconsistently, creating opportunities for bias. The article highlights this as a structural factor that 'invites bias.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity (competition judging category)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH competition that solicited methods to measure peer review bias awarded categories including 'creativity'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition judged submissions in multiple categories; Lee and Erosheva won first place in the creativity category, indicating 'creativity' was an explicit evaluation dimension for that competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of demographic disparities in funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and document demographic differences in funding outcomes (example: a 2011 Science paper showed Black investigators are ten percent less likely than White investigators to receive major NIH research grants, even controlling for factors like education, past training, and productivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical analyses to detect whether funding disparities exist across demographic groups; the Science finding is cited as motivation for the NIH competition and for further methodological work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for confounding variables in bias analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses of differential funding should control for covariates such as education, past training, and productivity when estimating bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Science result cited accounted for those factors; rigorous bias-detection studies should likewise adjust for plausible confounders to isolate bias effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multivariate statistical approaches to detect bias patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply sophisticated multivariate data analysis that examines a number of variables in how criteria are weighted to make sense of patterns indicating bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erosheva proposed a multivariate approach that looks across many variables to understand how reviewers weigh criteria differently; such methods can reveal systematic patterns of bias that simpler analyses might miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include statistical expertise / interdisciplinary collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite or include statisticians (or other appropriate quantitative experts) when designing studies to measure peer review bias so the best study design and methods are used and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasizes the value of an unusual collaboration between a philosopher and a statistician: statistical consulting helped identify and justify optimal study design within a tight deadline. This is presented as a recommended practice for credible measurement efforts.
